memory_lessons.applicability: Serial uint32 popcount recurrence on the frozen GCC 14.2 target.
memory_lessons.claim: The builtin-count source 2212 measured 81.694 µs, while the factor-four unroll with naive counting measured 971.213 µs. This supports the count replacement as the major observed change, not an unroll benefit. The combination needs its own measurement.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Compare this complete integrated program with 2212 under the official protocol; retain the unroll only if its measured result improves the base.

proposal.hypothesis: Combining the measured GCC builtin population count from 2212 with T3's ordered factor-four unroll and scalar tail may reduce loop-control overhead. The factor-four trial with naive counting was much slower, so it does not establish a gain with this faster count; the combined program must be evaluated independently.

retained: Adapted the factor-four ordered inner-loop unroll and scalar tail from 01dca30e10394426, replacing its naive count with the builtin.
